messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime-prod: pod memory trending high across 3 nodes. Metric: kv_cache.size and continuous_batching.latency spiking. Paging on-call. Ticket created: INC-2027-1183.

mira: seeing huge KV cache growth in logs, looks correlated with the rollout we did 30m ago that enabled continuous batching by default for the transformer-7 model. memory RSS steadily climbs until OOM/killing.

devash: yeah I can reproduce locally with a sim load — if batching keeps extending prefixes the KV cache retention never hits GC. think we triggered an unbounded warmup.

jordan: autoscaler is reacting — HPA kicked from 4 -> 12 pods in last 8m, then dropped to 6, then back to 11. looks like thrash. request rate stable so it's metric-driven on per-pod memory. we should stop the feedback loop.

lee: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip continuous_batching=false via runtime config to stop growing kv entries, 2) tighten HPA target to avoid oscillation, 3) rollout restart to purge KV caches. Can we do 1 now?

devash: I'm patching the runtime config to disable continuous batching for the model group and set per-request batch.deadline_ms=50. Doing via admin API so it's reversible.

devash: ```bash
# toggle feature flag in prod control plane
curl -s -X POST "https://admin-internal.prod.redwood/api/v1/configs/runtime" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model_group":"transformer-7","continuous_batching":false,"batch_deadline_ms":50}'
```

mira: applied and confirmed in control plane. runtime config shows continuous_batching=false for transformer-7. Propagating to nodes (will take ~30s - 2m).

opsbot: HPA: observed metric spike. Current HPA config: min=4 max=20 memory-target=70%. Recommend adjusting target to 80% temporarily and increasing stabilizationWindowSeconds to 120 to reduce thrash.

jordan: agreed, patching HPA now to dampen reaction. Applying small change to stabilization window and target utilization.

jordan: ```yaml
# hpa-patch.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: runtime-pods
  namespace: prod
spec:
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: memory
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 80
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
```

jordan: applied hpa changes (kubectl apply -f hpa-patch.yaml) and increased CPU/memory limit on the runtime container for a quick buffer.

lee: rolling restart to flush existing KV stores in pods (one-by-one) to avoid mass reconnects: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime -n prod --field-selector=status.phase=Running` — I'll run with maxUnavailable=1.

lee: restarting pods now. Expect some in-flight requests to fail during handoff. Putting note in incident ticket to mark possible 503s.

opsbot: metric update: kv_cache.size trending down in last 90s. HPA scaling events reduced. Memory per-pod median dropping from 68% -> 45% in 3m.

mira: customer-facing note: a handful of high-throughput customers in eu-west1 hit elevated 5xxs for ~6m around the peak. We should message CS with timeline + remediation.

noah: taking over as on-call for next shift. Status summary for handoff: continuous_batching disabled for transformer-7, batch_deadline_ms set to 50, HPA target bumped to 80% and stabilization window 120s, rollout restart in progress, kv_cache.size decreasing, autoscale events reduced. Incident ticket INC-2027-1183 updated with runbook and commands executed.

mira: follow-ups for postmortem: - root cause triage of why continuous batching allowed unbounded KV retention, - add hard caps on per-model KV entries, - add telemetry for kv entry churn, - add unit/regression test for warmup GC.

devash: also propose a fast-fail guard: if kv_cache.size per-pod > threshold for X seconds, temporarily disable continuous batching via control plane automation.

noah: ack. I'll draft the postmortem skeleton and assign owners. Logging the action items in the ticket and tagging @platform-team @eng-runtime.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: INC-2027-1183: Mitigated — memory and kv cache metrics stabilized. Impact: transient 5xxs for a subset of customers (~6m). Next: postmortem and long-term mitigation.

mira: :thumbsup: handing off to noah. If anything flips back, ping with @pager to wake me.

noah: thanks — I'll keep an eye on the dashboard and circle back with a summary in 30m.
